--- page 1 ---
Cover: "Anticipatory Humanitarian Action – Pilot: 2020 Monsoon floods in Bangladesh". Endorsed by RC and agencies 25 June 2020; pre-approved by ERC 26 June 2020; version 26 June 2020. No figure.
--- page 2 ---
Table of contents (narrative, no figure): Exec summary, 1 Introduction, 2 Forecast and triggers, 3 Anticipatory Actions (summary table p9), 4 Pre-agreed financing, 5 Learning, Annexes 1-3, 5-9.
--- page 3 ---
Executive summary, narrative text, no figure. Key facts: Jamuna River, 5 districts; two-stage trigger. Stage I (readiness): GloFAS and/or FFWC 15-day forecast, 10-day lead, >50% likely to cross 100,000 m3/s at Bahadurabad over 3 days (1-in-5-yr RP). Stage II (activation): FFWC 5-day forecast water level at Bahadurabad crosses government "Danger Level" + 0.85 m. 61,500 households get US$53 cash (55,500 WFP, 6,000 BDRCS). FAO 14,000 households; UNFPA ~15,000 women and girls. CERF US$5.34M ($4.25M WFP incl. RCRC subgrant, $500,000 FAO, $589,084 UNFPA); released at first 10-day trigger, full use at 5-day trigger.
--- page 4 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Introduction: ~1/4 of Bangladesh inundated in average year; severe flood every 4-5 years may cover >60%; ~80% of rainfall June-October. Pilot districts: Bogura (Bogra), Gaibandha, Kurigram, Jamalpur, Sirajgonj. Four scale-up areas: finance, reach, sectoral scope, learning.
--- page 5 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Forecasts: GloFAS 10-day probabilistic (T-10), FFWC 5-day deterministic (T-5). Severe shock = 1-in-5-yr RP; vulnerability threshold >40% population affected or 20% household assets damaged. Stage I/II trigger definitions repeated (Bahadurabad, 100,000 m3/s, Danger Level +0.85 m). Footnote: HCTT contingency plan triggers at water level at/above danger level up to 1 m in at least 3 observation points incl. Bahadurabad (>=2M people exposed, 10% displaced, 5,000 ha cropland). An intervention map (flood depth + population) identifies unions where impact crosses limit.
--- page 6 ---
Table: Monitoring of trigger and information flow (Who/What/How/When). BDRCS-led forecast monitoring team (Hassan) monitors GLOFAS and FFWC twice daily from June 2020 in a log sheet; confirms 10-day pre-activation or 5-day activation and notifies RC/RCO, UN agencies, OCHA via email and WhatsApp with an intervention map; CERF sends pre-approved approval letters immediately at 10-day warning (or 5-day trigger without prior 10-day warning); RC/RCO may call meeting. Known challenge: FFWC data access at peak; historic analysis says pre-activation is 40% likely to be followed by activation; in 30% of cases pre-activation not followed by activation; remaining cases 5-day activation without 10-day pre-activation.
--- page 7 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Cash: WFP 61,500 families target (55,500 WFP + 6,000 RCRC subgrant), one-off unconditional 4,500 taka (~US$53) via bKash (RCRC via Bangladesh Post Office). Beneficiaries from pre-existing lists; unions ranked by RCRC map combining flood depth, exposure, vulnerability.
--- page 8 ---
Narrative text, no figure. RCRC needs 10-day pre-activation to proceed. FAO 14,000 households (livestock services; asset storage). UNFPA 14,922 women and girls (dignity kits, MHM kits, RH kits). Challenges: limited time, list inclusion/exclusion errors, bKash delays, duplication (targeting team), RCRC volunteer/BPO constraints.
--- page 9 ---
Narrative text, no figure (continuation of challenges bullets): subgranting complexity; no 10-day trigger but 5-day trigger means very short delivery windows; FAO actions within 10 days before flood.
--- page 10 ---
Table: Summary of Anticipatory Actions (Agency/Reach/Funds; beneficiary selection criteria; actions by stage). WFP [55,500 households] [$4.25M from CERF]: Stage I (between 10-day readiness and 5-day activation) resilience team review, coordination, inform beneficiaries to keep phones active, verify bank accounts; Stage II (after 5-day trigger) distribute cash to FSP account, instruct transfers, inform beneficiaries. Selection: women-headed HHs, extremely poor, flood experience in last 5 years, casual labour, no regular income, many dependents, landless/marginal, elderly >60, weak housing. FAO [14,000 households] [$500,000 from CERF]: Stage I awareness raising, livestock services support with IFRC & WFP; selection: <=5 head livestock, landless, low income, single-parent, limited services.
--- page 11 ---
Table continued. FAO Stage II: real-time info dissemination, village flood management committees, livestock packages at community animal aggregation centers (feed, water, vaccines, vet services), watertight storage drums/ropes for grain and seeds. UNFPA [15,000 women and girls] [$589,084 from CERF]: selection women of reproductive age 15-49, pregnant/lactating, GBV survivors, transgender/Hijra, adolescents, women with disabilities; Stage I: dignity kits, MHM kits, RH kits transport/distribution planning with GBV flashcards.
--- page 12 ---
Table continued. UNFPA Stage II: distribute dignity kits (women/girls 15-49), MHM kits (adolescent girls 10-18), RH kits to District hospitals and Upazila Health Complexes in three districts; CMR refresher training. RCRC [6,000 HH as CERF sub-grantee]: selection by house type, flood experience, dependents, family structure, livelihood; Stage I: orientation, beneficiary list via ODK form, coordinate with DDM/MoDMR and Bangladesh Post Office, deploy NDRT; Stage II: analyse FFWC forecast raster, prioritise union list, handover to BPO for cash, evacuation support, monitoring.
--- page 13 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Pre-agreed financing: USG/ERC up to US$80M for AA pilots 2020-21 (drought Somalia, Ethiopia, Malawi, Chad; cholera; Bangladesh floods). Past CERF allocations: 2017 $3.4M (6.9M affected, 300,000 targeted, $12M required); 2019 $5.3M (7.6M affected, 736,000 targeted, $27M required); >$95M since 2007. Pilot: $5,339,084 set aside; projects approved at first 10-day trigger; season ends 31 October 2020 (unspent funds reimbursed if no 5-day trigger); only one guaranteed activation; pilot time-bound to two years.
--- page 14 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Links to other financing: WFP FbF in Kurigram since 2018 (~6,000 households); BDRCS 6,000 families via CERF + 3,500 via DREF; SUFAL (ECHO) project. Challenges: short financing timelines, reimbursement/pre-finance for subgrantees.

Narrative text, no figure. Learning: three ways (process learning/action learning reviews, agency M&E, independent evaluation); ad-hoc committee convened by OCHA; 2 action learning reviews (30-90 min) with CDP; 8-10 stakeholder interviews.

Narrative text, no figure. RCRC/BDRCS monitoring/PDM and impact evaluation; UNFPA joint monitoring and lessons workshop. Independent evaluation commissioned by OCHA if 5-day trigger reached, based on ToC (Annex 9).
--- page 19 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Evaluation indicators: cost per beneficiary lower; beneficiaries reached faster, <10% reporting severe hardship; lower mortality, morbidity, food insecurity, asset losses vs control group; large household survey months after.

--- page 23 ---
Annex 3 Table 1 (forecast skill): GLOFAS global, probabilistic discharge/return period on Brahmaputra (Jamuna) at Bahadurabad, lead 1-15 days, skill 10-day R2 0.760, 15-day R2 0.610 (limited data, 1 year). FFWC short-term deterministic, water level at 52 locations, lead 1-5 days, 5-day R2 0.72, FAR (5 days) 0.29. FFWC probabilistic, water level mean +sd/mean/mean-SD, lead 1-10 days, 10-day R2 0.61 (FFWC annual report 2016). Text: FFWC 5-day forecast evaluated at Sariakandi station for Danger Level: predicted 67% of floods, 29% false alarms. Trigger: >1-in-5-yr RP, >40% affected population or 20% HH asset damage.
--- page 24 ---
Figure 1 (chart): Impact on household assets (y, 0-100%) vs flood depth in metres (x, 0-2.75 m) for OS Embankment, Erosion, Char land; exponential fits: y=0.0736e^(1.0175x), R2=0.974 (Char) and y=0.0683e^(0.9201x), R2=0.9919 (OS Embk). ~10% impact at ~0.5 m rising to ~65-100% at ~2.5 m. Source: survey and KII.
Figure 2 (map): Vulnerability index of unions in Jamuna flood plain area, districts labelled Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, Rongpur, Gaibandha, Sherpur, Bogra, Jamalpur, Sirajganj, Tangail, Pabna, Manikganj; scale 27.70-91.99 (highest, red/orange, in north: Kurigram, Gaibandha, Jamalpur, Sherpur; lower, yellow/green, in south).
Text: Danger Level ≈ 1-in-5 yr RP (agricultural fields); houses ~1 m higher, flooding to houses ≈ 1-in-10 yr; DL+1.0 m at Bahadurabad = extreme event; DL+1 m causes ~25% HH asset damage; historic data: big floods ≥25% house damage and 40% affected population.
--- page 25 ---
Figure 3 (flow): Methodology 'where to activate': impacted unions cross the limits → overlay on union-wise Vulnerability Index map → rank unions based on vulnerability by exposures.
Figure 4 (three maps of the Jamuna flood plain unions): (1) average forecast flood depth (m) per union, scale low 0.0433583 to high 3.75614; (2) affected population, limit 40% (classes 0-40% grey up to 90-100% red); (3) impacted HH asset, limit 25% (grey 7.0-25% to red 85-100%), concentrated along the river corridor. Text: Fig 5 uses 1-in-5-yr threshold 100,000 m3/s GloFAS; 3 consecutive days above threshold.
--- page 26 ---
Figure 5 (time-series, ~1987-2019): top panel GloFAS water discharge at Bahadurabad (y 0-140,000 m3/s) with dashed 100,000 m3/s threshold; bottom panel FFWC water level (y ~19.5-21 m) with dashed FFWC water level threshold (~20.35 m); blue = below, red = above threshold; arrows mark simulated historical pre-activations (green, GloFAS; ~7 arrows) and activations (blue, FFWC; ~5 arrows incl. ~1988, ~2012-2017, 2019). Findings since 1987: GloFAS pre-activation followed by FFWC activation twice (1988, 2019); GloFAS reached but FFWC below threshold 3 times (1995, 2003, 2004); FFWC above threshold but GloFAS not 3 times (2013, 2016, 2017). Pre-activation 30%/40% likely followed by activation (text states both; 2 of 5 = 40% of activations preceded by pre-activation); GloFAS expected to miss 60% of FFWC activations.

--- page 28 ---
Annex 9 (diagram, DRAFT): UN-OCHA Anticipatory Action Pilots Theory of Change "Acting earlier for a more impactful response". Activities (i-v: promote AA, country analysis of risks/triggers, joint planning, review agency systems for rapid funds flow, central M&E framework) → Outputs (a. Early Action Plans with automated decision points approved by RCs; b. IF TRIGGERED, CERF funds provided at expected time to UN agencies; c. high-quality lessons learned/evidence publicly available) → Intermediate outcomes (1-7: improved coordination; improved decision-making; more cost-effective response; more timely response; lower welfare impacts on vulnerable households; improved evidence base; more organisations follow CERF's lead) → Long-term outcomes (A-D: CERF embeds AA as default; sectors adopt similar systems; financing shifts to mitigate impacts; increased dignity) → Impact: reduced impact of global crises on poor and vulnerable people, reduced humanitarian needs. Blue shading = outcomes only appearing if early action triggered. Underlying problems: slow crisis response, uncoordinated responses, "wait and see" architecture.
